papers.title: A Model-Driven Approach for Design and Generation of Collaborative Cross-platform Graphical Editors in Engineering Education
papers.abstract: This work introduces a Model-Driven Development (MDD) approach for the design and automatic generation of collaborative cross-platform and multitouch graphical editors tailored to engineering education. The proposed method facilitates the creation of customizable graphical editors, aiming to balance ease of use with the flexibility afforded by model-based design. While a foundational understanding of modelling tools is advantageous during the initial development phase, the resulting editors provides an inclusive user experience across diverse devices and operating environments. A preliminary evaluation involving university professors has been conducted to assess the effectiveness of the approach. The results underscore several strengths, notably the high degree of automation and the support for collaborative learning scenarios. Nonetheless, the evaluation also revealed limitations, including usability issues and dependence on specific integrated development environments (e.g., Eclipse). Overall, the proposed approach contributes to the advancement of scalable and innovative modelling tools in engineering education, fostering active learning and enhanced conceptual comprehension of modelling languages.

summary_en.motivation: The work aims to simplify the creation of customizable collaborative graphical editors for engineering education.
summary_en.method: A model-driven development approach is used to automatically generate cross-platform multitouch editors from models.
summary_en.result: A preliminary professor-based evaluation indicates strong automation and collaborative support but reveals usability and IDE-dependence limitations.
summary_en.validation: Validation relies on a preliminary qualitative evaluation with university professors rather than quantitative or simulation-based testing.

papers.title: BAYESIAN OPTIMIZATION OF CRYOPROTECTANT MIXTURES WITH ROBOTIC AUTOMATION

llm.relevance_to_user: 该文用贝叶斯优化加速冷冻保护剂配方筛选，属于实验设计优化而非FEA代理建模，与植入物力学仿真方向仅方法层面弱相关。
llm.why_not_core: It applies Bayesian optimization to experimental cryoprotectant formulation with robotic automation, with no FEA surrogate, no simulation sampling, no implant mechanics, and no biomechanical context.

summary_zh.motivation: 冷冻保护剂配方组合空间大，传统试错筛选效率低。
summary_zh.method: 结合机器人自动化实验平台与贝叶斯优化迭代搜索配方空间。
summary_zh.result: 在较少实验轮次内定位到较优保护剂混合配方。
summary_zh.validation: 体外细胞或材料实验验证配方效果。

summary_en.motivation: The vast combinatorial space of cryoprotectant formulations makes conventional trial-and-error screening inefficient.
summary_en.method: A robotic automation platform is coupled with Bayesian optimization to iteratively search the formulation space.
summary_en.result: Promising cryoprotectant mixtures are identified within a reduced number of experimental rounds.
summary_en.validation: Formulation performance is assessed through in vitro cell or material experiments.

papers.title: Comparative Peri-Implant Tissue Responses of Zirconia and Titanium Implant Systems Under Functional Loading: An In Vivo Split-Mouth Study.
papers.abstract: AIM: To compare peri-implant tissue responses around zirconia and titanium implant systems under functional loading in vivo. MATERIALS AND METHODS: In four male beagles with a split-mouth design, mandibular premolars were extracted and, after 8 weeks, two-piece bone-level titanium and one-piece tissue-level niobium-stabilised yttria-partially stabilised zirconia implants were placed contralaterally (n = 3/system/animal). Implant placement was at Week 0, restorations were delivered at Week 8 and final evaluation occurred at Week 24. Probing depth (PD) and bleeding on probing (BOP) were assessed at 20 and 24 weeks; implant stability, gingival crevicular fluid cytokines and subgingival microbiota were examined at Week 24; and bone-to-implant contact (BIC) and bone area (BA) within threads were checked histologically after sacrificing the animals. The animal was the statistical unit. RESULTS: Exploratory paired analyses showed lower mean PD and BOP around zirconia than titanium (p = 0.044 and p = 0.006, respectively) at the functional loading phase. No clear between-system differences were detected in implant stability or radiographic, cytokine/chemokine, targeted microbial or BIC outcomes. MCP-1, IL-6 and TNF-α were numerically lower around zirconia, with uncertain estimates. Higher mean BA was observed around zirconia and was exploratory. CONCLUSIONS: Exploratory differences in PD and BOP were observed between the systems; both demonstrated osseointegration under functional loading. The findings, however, do not establish material-specific clinical advantages.

llm.relevance_to_user: 这是一项锆与钛种植体动物实验，与增材制造多孔结构、应力遮挡或LPBF力学测试无关。
llm.why_not_core: This is an in vivo animal study of zirconia vs titanium dental implant soft-tissue responses with no LPBF fabrication, no porous architecture, no stress-shielding or stiffness-matching analysis, and no mechanical/fatigue testing.

summary_zh.motivation: 比较锆与钛种植体在功能负载下的种植体周围组织反应。
summary_zh.method: 四只比格犬分口设计，对侧植入钛与锆种植体，8周后修复，24周评估。
summary_zh.result: 锆种植体探诊深度与出血指数较低，但骨结合与稳定性无明确差异。
summary_zh.validation: 动物活体实验结合组织学与临床指标评估。

summary_en.motivation: To determine whether zirconia and titanium dental implant systems elicit different peri-implant tissue responses under functional loading.
summary_en.method: A split-mouth design in four beagles placed contralateral titanium and niobium-stabilized zirconia implants, with restorations at week 8 and evaluation through week 24 using clinical, cytokine, microbiological, and histological measures.
summary_en.result: Exploratory paired analyses indicated lower probing depth and bleeding on probing around zirconia, while implant stability, radiographic, cytokine, microbial, and bone-to-implant contact outcomes showed no clear between-system differences.
summary_en.validation: In vivo animal experiment with histological and clinical assessment.
